name: Húszashívásos Tarokk
description: Húszashívásos Tarokk is a Hungarian Tarokk variant featuring a unique bidding system where players bid to win 20 or more tricks. It is a point-trick game with a 42-card Tarot deck, featuring complex bidding and partnership dynamics.

overview.description: Húszashívásos Tarokk is a Hungarian Tarokk variant featuring a unique bidding system where players bid to win 20 or more tricks. It is a point-trick game with a 42-card Tarot deck, featuring complex bidding and partnership dynamics.

history.origins: Húszashívásos Tarokk is a Hungarian variant of Tarot card games that evolved from the French Tarot tradition. It became popular in Hungary in the 19th and early 20th centuries.
timeline: 15th Century: Tarot cards originate in Italy and France.
18th-19th Century: Tarot games spread to Central Europe.
Early 1900s: Hungarian Tarokk variants develop distinct rules.
Present: Still played in Hungarian card game clubs.
history.cultural: Tarokk games hold a special place in Hungarian card game culture, with dedicated clubs and tournaments.
history.evolution: The game developed its unique 'húszashívásos' (twenty-calling) bidding system, where players compete to win at least 20 tricks.

setup.deck: 42-card Tarokk deck (Tarot pack): 4 suits of 8 cards each, plus 22 tarot cards (trumps).
setup.dealing: Deal 9 cards to each player. The remaining 6 cards form the talon.

rules.objective: Win the bidding and capture at least 20 tricks to fulfill the contract.
rules.gameplay: 1. Bidding: Players bid to win 20 or more tricks. The highest bidder becomes the declarer. 2. The declarer takes the talon and discards 6 cards. 3. Trick play: Players must follow suit if possible. Tarot cards act as trumps. 4. Scoring: Points are awarded based on tricks won and contract fulfillment.
keyRules: Must follow suit if possible; can play any tarot if unable to follow
Tarot cards are permanent trumps, ranked by number
The declarer must win at least 20 tricks to fulfill contract
The talon is taken by the highest bidder who discards 6 cards

strategy.basic: Count the tarot cards - there are 22 trumps total. Save high trumps for important tricks.
strategy.intermediate: Bid aggressively when you have 8+ tarot cards. The talon can significantly improve your hand.
strategy.advanced: Card counting is essential - track which tarots have been played. Signal your partner through card play patterns.
tips: The Skiz (Tarot I) is the highest card and always wins
Save your high tarots for tricks you need to win
Watch your partner's discards for signals

scoring.winCondition: Win the bidding and capture at least the bid number of tricks (minimum 20).
